doc: Categories and states over the Hierarchical Requirement Designer's binding, hierarchical-requirement.fbl#markdown, in the Markdown file (User Story 8; FR-030, FR-031). category and state are word slots of a requirement's group words, after tags in the rule's attributes, each holding the first word of the group its word expression matches (FBL 0.7 section 4.6), so a second category: or state: word does not count and stays in the group as written: REQ-0004's category is legal, and its category:technical counts for nothing. REQ-0005 writes category:Technical, which names the member technical, ignoring case (DESL 0.2 section 7.7.2); legal names no member and is an implicit member of the category list. read lists the body's elements; the lists' members are stated in list/, which reads the same body through a registration. Each step is one operation of hierarchical-requirement.des, given as the model changes it makes, followed by its undo, except that the two removals on REQ-0003 are made one after the other and undone in reverse. An unset (clearCategory, clearState) is given as a set to null, since FBL's model changes have no unset (FBL section 11.2). A rename over several carriers is one transaction of several changes, of which the fixture's edit holds the first and x-transaction all (FBL section 15.3 gives an edit one change). The file has CRLF endings.

attributes.title: A customer orders without signing in.
An order is confirmed by e-mail.
An order can be cancelled within an hour.
Orders are kept for seven years.
A parcel is tracked from the warehouse to the door.

steps.doc: setCategory on REQ-0002 with functional: category holds no word, so the new word is an insert-key of one space and category:functional right after the last word of the group held by category or by a slot listed before it in the rule's attributes on the same group, which is tags' #mail (FBL 0.7 section 6.3, a word a set adds). So the category stands after the tags and before state:proposed.

steps.doc: clearCategory on REQ-0003 (unset of category): a removed word is a remove-key of the word and the whitespace before it, here category:technical and the space after the title (FBL 0.7 section 6.3, a removed word). The binding gives category no empty option, whose default for a string is keep (FBL section 5.2), which would write an empty value; the reading taken is that a word slot has no empty value to write, since category: alone is no word the slot reads, so the removal is the remove-key that section 6.3 gives a removed word.

steps.doc: renameCategory on technical with engineering: the operation sets the category of every requirement whose category is technical in any case, then the member's name, in one transaction (hierarchical-requirement.des, renameCategory; DESL 0.2 section 7.7.2). The carriers are REQ-0003 and REQ-0005, whose category:Technical names the member too; each is a replace-value of its word's group value (FBL 0.7 section 6.3). REQ-0004 is no carrier: its category is legal, and its second word category:technical is no value and stays as written. The member's new name writes the registration in the same edit: list/ shows those splices, which write the whole category list since it is absent (DESL 0.2 section 5.5).
